label: Double-yolked eggs with fused yolks yield four-legged, four-winged chicks
claim: In double-yolked eggs, if the yolks are separated by a membrane two normal chicks result, but if the yolks are continuous the chick is monstrous, with one body and head but four legs and four wings.
quote: when the yolks are continuous, with no division between them, the chickens produced are monstrous, having one body and head but four legs and four wings

label: Hermaphrodite genitals occur in humans and especially in goats
claim: Animals are sometimes born with both male and female genitals; this occurs in humans and especially in goats.
quote: Again, they may have the generative parts doubled, the one being male, the other female; this is known in men and especially in goats.

label: No animal is born without a heart or wholly without a liver
claim: No animal has ever been born without a heart or entirely without a liver, though animals are born without a spleen, with two spleens or with one kidney.
quote: No animal, indeed, has ever been born without a heart, but they are born without a spleen or with two spleens or with one kidney; there is no case again of total absence of the liver, but there are cases of its being incomplete.

label: Large animals bear few young, small animals many
claim: Among walking, flying and swimming animals alike, large animals produce few young and small animals many, because in large animals the nutriment goes to increasing the body.
quote: And not only in animals that walk but also in those that fly or swim the large ones produce few, the small many, for the same reason.
scope: animals generally: mammals, birds and fishes

label: Human gestation alone is irregular, seven to ten months
claim: Man alone among animals has an irregular gestation period: children are born from seven to ten months, and eight-month children survive, though less often than the rest.
quote: On account of this it results that in man alone among animals the period of gestation is irregular; whereas the period is fixed in the rest, there are several periods in man, for children are born at seven months and at ten months and at the times between, for even those of eight months do live though less often than the rest.

label: Women and mares alone accept the male during pregnancy
claim: Women and mares are the only animals that admit the male during gestation.
quote: therefore women and mares are the only animals which admit the male during gestation

label: Hares superfetate
claim: Superfetation (conceiving a second litter while already pregnant) occurs naturally in hares, because they are small, bear many young and are rich in semen.
quote: For superfoetation occurs in these animals, since they are not large and they bear many young (for they have many toes and the many-toed animals bear many), and they are spermatic.

label: Hoofed animals bear young complete, most many-toed animals incomplete
claim: Among viviparous animals, solid-hoofed and cloven-footed animals bear their young fully formed, while most many-toed animals bear them imperfect (many born blind).
quote: Some of the vivipara produce their young imperfect, others perfect; the one-hoofed and cloven-footed perfect, most of the many-toed imperfect.
scope: viviparous quadrupeds: ungulates versus fissipeds (dog, wolf, fox, bear, lion), with the pig as exception

label: Young swallows' eyes regrow after being put out
claim: If the eyes of nestling swallows are put out, they recover their sight, because the birds are still developing and the eyes grow afresh.
quote: Hence if the eyes of swallows while still young be put out they recover their sight again, for the birds are still developing, not yet developed, when the injury is inflicted, so that the eyes grow and sprout afresh.

label: In humans males are more often born defective than females
claim: In man, males are more often born defective than females, but this is not so in other animals.
quote: In man males are more often born defective than females, but in the other animals this is not the case.

label: Females develop slower in the womb but mature and age faster after birth
claim: In man the female develops more slowly than the male in the womb, but after birth reaches puberty, prime and old age sooner than the male.
quote: For while within the mother the female takes longer in developing, but after birth everything is perfected more quickly in females than in males; I mean, for instance, puberty, the prime of life, and old age.

label: Nursing women neither menstruate nor conceive
claim: While women are suckling, menstruation naturally does not occur and they do not conceive; if they do conceive, the milk dries up, because milk and menses are the same secretion.
quote: While women are suckling children the catamenia do not occur according to Nature, nor do they conceive; if they do conceive, the milk dries up.

label: All animals are naturally born head first
claim: The natural birth of all animals is head first, because the parts above the umbilical cord are larger and heavier.
quote: The natural birth of all animals is head-foremost, because the parts above the umbilical cord are larger than those below.

label: Man lives longer than any animal except the elephant
claim: Man lives longer than any animal for which there is credible evidence, except the elephant.
quote: Man lives a longer time than any animal of which we have any credible experience except the elephant
scope: humans compared with other animals, especially mammals

label: Gestation length is caused by the size of the offspring, not by lifespan
claim: Gestation length roughly corresponds to lifespan only incidentally; its real cause is the size of the offspring, since large masses take long to perfect.
quote: but the cause of the time of gestation is the size of the offspring. For it is not easy for large masses to arrive at their perfection in a small time

label: Horses gestate a year, humans ten months, elephants two years
claim: Horses and their kin carry their young for a year, man at most ten months, and elephants for two years.
quote: That is why horses and animals akin to them, though living a shorter time than man, yet carry their young longer; for the time in the former is a year, but in the latter ten months at the outside. For the same reason also the time is long in elephants; they carry their young two years on account of their excessive size.
scope: horse, ass and kin (Equus), humans, elephants

label: Eye colour has no final cause unless characteristic of the kind
claim: Features not characteristic of a whole kind, such as an individual's eye colour, do not exist for a final cause but arise of necessity from the material and the efficient cause.
quote: The eye for instance exists for a final cause, but it is not blue for a final cause unless this condition be characteristic of the kind of animal.
scope: variable traits of animals, especially in man

label: Embryos sleep most of the time but wake briefly in the womb
claim: Embryos sleep most of the time, though they are found to wake briefly even in the womb, which is why newborns spend most of their time asleep.
quote: But nevertheless they are found to wake even in the womb (this is clear in dissections and in the ovipara), and then they immediately fall into a sleep again. This is why after birth also they spend most of their time in sleep.
scope: animal embryos and newborns, including humans

label: Infants laugh only in sleep, not awake
claim: Infants do not laugh when awake, but while asleep they both laugh and cry.
quote: When awake infants do not laugh, but while asleep they both laugh and cry.

label: All newborn children have bluish eyes that later change colour
claim: The eyes of all children are bluish at birth and later change to their permanent colour, which is not seen in other animals.
quote: The eyes of all children are bluish immediately after birth; later on they change to the colour which is to be theirs permanently. But in the case of other animals this is not visible.

label: Only horses and humans have eyes of different colours
claim: Of animals other than man, the horse has the greatest variety of eye colour and some horses have two differently coloured eyes; this is seen in no other animal, but sometimes in man.
quote: Of the other animals the horse has the greatest variety of colour in the eye, for some of them are actually heteroglaucous; this phenomenon is not to be seen in any of the other animals, but man is sometimes heteroglaucous.

label: Blue eyes see poorly by day, dark eyes poorly by night
claim: Blue eyes are not keen-sighted by day and dark eyes are not keen-sighted by night.
quote: We must suppose the same cause also to be responsible for the fact that blue eyes are not keen-sighted by day nor dark eyes by night.

label: Cataract attacks blue eyes more, night-blindness dark eyes
claim: Cataract affects blue-eyed people more, while nyctalopia affects dark-eyed people more.
quote: Cataract attacks the blue-eyed more, but what is called ‘nyctalopia’ the dark-eyed.

label: Animals with deep-set eyes see far, those with prominent eyes do not
claim: Animals with prominent eyes do not see well at a distance, whereas those whose eyes lie deep in the head can see distant things.
quote: A proof of this is that animals with prominent eyes do not see well at a distance, whereas those which have their eyes lying deep in the head can see things at a distance

label: The seal has no external ears, only hearing passages
claim: The seal, though a viviparous quadruped, has no external ears but only passages for hearing, because it lives in the water.
quote: The workmanship of Nature is admirable also in the seal, for though a viviparous quadruped it has no ears but only passages for hearing. This is because its life is passed in the water

label: Only humans visibly go grey with age, and to a lesser degree horses
claim: Humans go grey on the head as they age, but this is not visible in practically any other animal except, to some extent, the horse.
quote: Human beings also go grey on the head as they grow old, but this is not visible in practically any other animal, though more so in the horse than others.

label: Men go bald in front and grey first at the temples
claim: Men go bald on the front of the head but turn grey first on the temples; no one goes bald first on the temples or the back of the head.
quote: Men go bald on the front of the head, but turn grey first on the temples; no one goes bald first on these or on the back of the head.

label: Peoples of moist cold lands are straight-haired, of hot dry lands curly
claim: Peoples living in moist air, such as the Scythians and Thracians, are straight-haired, while Ethiopians and others in hot countries are curly-haired because their brains and the surrounding air are dry.
quote: For this reason the Scythians on the Black Sea and the Thracians are straight-haired, for both they themselves and the environing air are moist, whereas the Aethiopians and men in hot countries are curly-haired, for their brains and the surrounding air are dry.

label: Deep-water sea-urchins have large, hard spines because of cold
claim: Sea-urchins that live in deep, cold water (sixty fathoms or more) have large, hard spines though their bodies are small.
quote: For these, too, though small themselves, have large and hard spines because the sea in which they live is cold on account of its depth (for they are found in sixty fathoms and even more).

label: Women and eunuchs do not go bald
claim: Women do not go bald, since like children they produce no seminal secretion, and eunuchs do not go bald because they change into the female condition.
quote: Women do not go bald because their nature is like that of children, both alike being incapable of producing seminal secretion. Eunuchs do not become bald, because they change into the female condition.

label: Hair covered by hats goes grey sooner
claim: Greying is a kind of decay, so hair protected by hats or other coverings, being sheltered from the winds, goes grey sooner.
quote: hair protected by hats or other coverings goes grey sooner (for the winds prevent decay and the protection keeps off the winds)

label: White individuals occur in normally uniform-coloured species
claim: Even in uniformly coloured kinds, white individuals occasionally arise when development is perverted, as has been seen in partridges, ravens, sparrows and bears.
quote: but still they do so change, for before now white individuals have been observed among partridges, ravens, sparrows, and bears.
scope: partridges, ravens, sparrows, bears and other uniformly coloured animals

label: Hot drinking water whitens hair, cold water darkens it
claim: Colour change in animals whose kind is many-coloured is due to the water they drink: hot waters make the hair white and cold waters make it dark.
quote: This is owing to the water which they drink, for hot waters make the hair white, cold makes it dark, an effect found also in plants.
scope: animals whose individuals are whole-coloured but whose kind is many-coloured (e.g. cattle, goats)

label: The belly is whiter in animals that are not uniformly coloured
claim: In all animals that are not uniformly coloured, the underside of the belly is whiter.
quote: Hence also in all animals not uniformly coloured all the part under the belly is whiter.

label: Females have higher voices than males, except in cattle
claim: In animals generally the female's voice is higher than the male's, most plainly in man, but in cattle the cow's voice is deeper than the bull's.
quote: in the other kinds of animals the voice of the female is higher than that of the male (this being especially plain in man, for Nature has given this faculty to him in the highest degree because he alone of animals makes use of speech and the voice is the material of speech), but in cattle the opposite obtains, for the voice of cows is deeper than that of bulls.

label: A bone is found in the heart of some bulls
claim: A bone is found in the heart of some bulls.
quote: That the heart of bulls is of such a nature is shown by the fact that a bone is actually found in some of them

label: Castrated animals take on a female voice and character
claim: All animals, when castrated, change to the female character and utter a voice like that of females.
quote: All animals when castrated change to the female character, and utter a voice like that of the females because the sinewy strength in the principle of the voice is relaxed.
scope: male animals with testes, including humans

label: The pig does not shed its teeth; lions shed only their canines
claim: The pig does not shed its teeth, and some carnivores, such as lions, shed no teeth except the canines.
quote: Yet the pig also suckles but does not shed its teeth, and, further, all the animals with carnivorous dentition suckle, but some of them do not shed any teeth except the canines, e.g. lions.
scope: pigs and carnivores such as lions

label: Nature never fails nor does anything in vain
claim: Nature never fails nor does anything in vain, so far as is possible in each case.
quote: Now we assume, basing our assumption upon what we see, that Nature never fails nor does anything in vain so far as is possible in each case.

label: Young fed hotter milk cut their teeth sooner
claim: Suckling itself does not form the teeth, but the heat of the milk speeds them: young that receive hotter milk grow their teeth more quickly.
quote: A proof of this is that even in suckling animals those young which enjoy hotter milk grow their teeth quicker, heat being conducive to growth.

label: The last human grinders erupt around age twenty
claim: The grinding teeth keep growing for a long time, the last of them cutting the gum at about twenty years of age and sometimes in old age.
quote: A proof of this is that even the flat teeth grow for a long time, the last of them cutting the gum at about twenty years of age; indeed in some cases the last teeth have been grown in quite old age.
